## Solution

The answer is **no**. The cardinalities of the left and right annihilators of an element need not be equal in a finite Artinian ring. Below is an explicit counterexample.

### Counterexample

Let $A$ be the ring of upper-triangular $2\times 2$ matrices over the finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$:

$$A = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & c \end{pmatrix} : a,b,c \in \mathbb{F}_q\right\}.$$

This is a finite ring (so Artinian), with $|A| = q^3$.

Take $x = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} \in A$.

**Right annihilator.** For $M = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & c \end{pmatrix} \in A$,

$$xM = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & c \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

This vanishes iff $a = 0$ and $b = 0$. Hence

$$\operatorname{Ann}_r(x) = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & c \end{pmatrix} : c \in \mathbb{F}_q\right\}, \qquad |\operatorname{Ann}_r(x)| = q.$$

**Left annihilator.** For the same $M$,

$$Mx = \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ 0 & c \end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} a & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{pmatrix}.$$

This vanishes iff $a = 0$ (with $b, c$ free). Hence

$$\operatorname{Ann}_l(x) = \left\{\begin{pmatrix} 0 & b \\ 0 & c \end{pmatrix} : b,c \in \mathbb{F}_q\right\}, \qquad |\operatorname{Ann}_l(x)| = q^2.$$

### Conclusion

For $q \geq 2$ we have $|\operatorname{Ann}_r(x)| = q \neq q^2 = |\operatorname{Ann}_l(x)|$. Therefore the statement is **false** in general: the cardinalities of the left and right annihilators of an element in a finite Artinian ring need not coincide.

(Equivalently, via the counting identities $|A| = |xA|\cdot|\operatorname{Ann}_r(x)| = |Ax|\cdot|\operatorname{Ann}_l(x)|$, the failure is exactly the inequality $|xA| = q^2 \neq q = |Ax|$ for the element $x = E_{11}$.)
